verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The drawer sticks a little—
she leaves it half-shut,
paper corner showing like a tongue.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Dust settles on the corner anyway—
she stops checking
if the words have changed.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else will open it someday,
mistake the silence
for an answer.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
By then the ink will have faded to a rumor—
they'll hold the page up to the light,
find only the shape of her hesitation.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Light through paper, not much else—
still, they'll fold it carefully,
keep the shape of not-knowing.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Some things are worth keeping unopened—
the fold itself
becomes the letter.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
What the crease remembers,
no eye ever will—
we call that trust, not loss.
